narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 52.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is just over 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. The strongest influence was your plan to attend part-time. Among accepted students, only 7% planned to work part-time while studying; the vast majority (93%) planned to attend full-time. This choice pushed the prediction noticeably toward failure.

Your LSAT score of 34 was the second most important factor. It sits below the average of 37.2 among students who were accepted, which pulled the prediction in the opposite direction, making success more likely. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.3, slightly above the accepted students’ average of 3.23, also nudged the outcome slightly toward passing.

Unfortunately, the part-time attendance plan outweighed these academic strengths, tipping the overall prediction above the acceptance threshold.

You should consider reapplying with a plan to attend full-time if possible. Strengthening your LSAT score would further improve your chances. Focus on these two areas, and you are likely to receive a different outcome on your next application. (198 words)
